| proven | **Scan waves over the cell graph** | Mechanics | A ping or sweep spreads outward cell by cell, confined by solid walls, building and then exhausting over time. The outgoing pulse is the visible wave: a continuous front with eased per-cell attack and decay, solved once into typed arrays in small time slices off the render loop. Active pings are loud and sharp, passive ones quiet and stale. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/perception/scan-waves)<br>test: test/scan.test.js: waves never enter solid cells and are confined to the connected open region; arrival = path distance / speed |
| proven | **Echo returns from identifiers** | Mechanics | Anything that identifies itself (you, devices, decoys, adversaries) becomes a new origin when the ping reaches it, and a second geodesic wave spreads out of it, invisibly. It is latched once against the cell you stand in when it reaches you, and then you see that echo field replayed in reverse, in its own hue: a front that starts on the ring through you and contracts onto the source, then a stale glimpse of where it was. One flag, echo.reveal on-arrival or live. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/perception/scan-waves)<br>test: test/scan-echo.test.js: the reversed front contracts monotonically from the receiver isochrone and ends at the source |
